title: COPD, respiratory failure and home oxygen
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's chronic lung disease and any respiratory failure or oxygen dependence.
note:
Chief Complaint
Increased shortness of breath and cough.

HPI
Pt is a 61 y/o male with a hx of COPD presenting for f/u. Pt reports acute exacerbation of symptoms over the past 3 days, characterized by increased dyspnea and productive cough. Pt reports feeling more short of breath than baseline. Pt currently uses home oxygen continuously at home.

Medication List
1. Prednisone 40mg daily
2. Tiotropium inhaler
3. Home oxygen (continuous)

Exam
General: Alert, in mild respiratory distress.
Vitals: HR 92, RR 22, SpO2 89% on 2L NC.
Lungs: Diminished breath sounds, scattered wheezes throughout.
CV: RRR, CTAB.
Ext: No edema noted.

Assessment
1. Acute exacerbation of COPD.
2. Chronic respiratory failure with hypoxia.

Plan
1. Start steroid burst: Prednisone 40mg PO daily for 5 days.
2. Continue current home oxygen regimen.
3. Follow up in 2 weeks to monitor symptoms.

Electronically signed, K. Nguyen, DO, 05/14/2026
explanations: COPD with an acute exacerbation: J44.1 (same HCC 280 as stable COPD, but a different code).
Chronic respiratory failure with hypoxia: J96.11 (HCC 213), plus Z99.81 for the home oxygen.

distractors.why: An acute exacerbation is documented: J44.1.
The provider diagnoses chronic respiratory failure: J96.11 (HCC 213).
Only chronic respiratory failure is documented.

hccs.label: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease/Interstitial Lung Disorders/and Other Chronic Lung Disorders
